column1: # Accepted differences between the DBC oracles (cantools <-> canmatrix) in scripts/selftest.py.
# A listed difference is reported as "known", never as "pass"; one whose scenario ran without showing it fails the run: remove the line. Columns (tab-separated):

column5: Data longer than the message (12 bytes for an 8-byte message): cantools decodes it (allow_excess), canmatrix rejects it (DecodingFrameLength). Both reject data that is too short.
Multiplexer value 3 selects no multiplexed signal: cantools rejects the frame ("expected multiplexer id 0, 1 or 2"), canmatrix decodes the signals that are not multiplexed.
S0 = 3 selects no branch: cantools rejects the frame, canmatrix decodes the signals that are not multiplexed.
canmatrix 1.3.3 cannot encode extended multiplexing (Frame.encode raises EncodingComplexMultiplexed); cantools can.

A PDU mapped at frame byte 2 (PDU-TO-FRAME-MAPPING START-POSITION 16): cantools 45.1.1 and canmatrix 1.3.3 both place its signals as if the PDU started at bit 0. AUTOSAR places them after the offset, so neither oracle can check a consumer here; the self-test records the oracles behaviour (scenario arxml-pdu-offset). AUTOSAR TPS System Template, PduToFrameMapping.startPosition.
canmatrix 1.3.3 reads only the selector of a MULTIPLEXED-I-PDU (named "Multiplexor", signed) and none of its signals; cantools is the oracle of multiplexed.arxml.
python-can CSV keeps only part of the fields of a frame (docs/LOG_FORMATS.md), so a round trip does not reproduce every frame.
